incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-36 relating to sociétés par actions simplifiées
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution et statuts de la société
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum paid-up capital of 1 EUR; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro Forma First Board Resolution of the proposed SAS: The initial shareholders and directors hereby unanimously resolve on [Date] as follows: (1) The share capital is fixed at [Amount] EUR and fully subscribed by the shareholders in the proportions set out in the articles of association; (2) The registered office is adopted at [Full Address], France, with the Board of Directors empowered to modify it in accordance with legal requirements; (3) The following officers are appointed with immediate effect and full powers of representation: President [Name], Directors [Names], and Secretary [Name]; (4) The articles of association are adopted in the form presented and authorised for filing with the commercial registry. This resolution is minuted and signed by all shareholders and directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public followed by Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and sign the articles of association including share capital, corporate object, and officer details before a French notary. Obtain notarized copies and shareholder declarations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amendments and re-submission to notary if queried

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Documents with Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via guichet unique or online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit notarized articles, shareholder list, and applicable fees. Request SIREN number and obtain receipt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Corrections within 15 days if application is incomplete or queried

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Legal Notices and Obtain RCS Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal Officiel de la République Française and Greffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the incorporation announcement in the Journal Officiel. Receive SIREN and SIRET numbers and extract Kbis.
Open corporate bank account using SIREN certificate. Register for corporate tax, VAT, and social security obligations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rejection and resubmission for missing or incorrect documentation

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence d'établissement de services de paiement

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique et de la Cohésion des Territoires
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No physical operations; compliance with digital data protection and cybersecurity standards

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office space compliance with fire safety, structural, and workplace regulations if any physical premises are used; virtual operations exempt

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), including the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and, for non-established businesses, the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE). Online tax services are provided through impots.gouv.fr; company formation and registration filings are submitted through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate or register the Société par Actions Simplifiée through the INPI Guichet unique. 2. Obtain the company SIREN and SIRET identifiers from the Registre national des entreprises. 3. Open the professional tax account on impots.gouv.fr using the legal entity details and registration certificate. 4. File the relevant corporate tax and VAT registration information with the competent SIE. 5. The DGFiP assigns the French VAT identification number, generally formatted as FR followed by two check characters and the nine-digit SIREN. 6. A foreign entity without a French establishment must register with the SIEE where French VAT obligations arise; a non-EU entity may require an accredited French tax representative unless an applicable legal or administrative exception applies. 7. A regulated card issuer must separately obtain the applicable payment-services or electronic-money authorization from the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR); tax registration does not authorize payment activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). A qualifying closely held SAS may elect temporary income-tax treatment under the statutory option applicable to certain newly formed companies, generally for a maximum of five fiscal years and subject to ownership, activity, age, and revenue conditions. There is no general United States-style check-the-box election. France applies statutory anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implementing EU ATAD requirements; those rules restrict deductions, deny duplicate deductions, or impose inclusion where relevant and are not elective classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), administered under the French General Tax Code and EU VAT rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the French domestic VAT exemption regime, the principal service threshold is EUR 37,500 of prior-year turnover, with a current-year tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250; the principal goods threshold is EUR 85,000, with a current-year tolerance threshold of EUR 93,500. Thresholds do not override mandatory registration for specified cross-border transactions, acquisitions, imports, or transactions outside the exemption regime. Financial services, payment transactions, credit, and certain related services may be VAT-exempt under Article 261 C of the French General Tax Code; taxable technology, management, platform, card-program, and ancillary services must be analyzed separately.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has no general real-time invoice-clearance requirement equivalent to a continuous transaction-control model. Domestic business-to-business e-invoicing is being phased in through approved or registered platforms: receipt capability is scheduled for all businesses from 1 September 2026; issuance is scheduled from 1 September 2026 for large and intermediate enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises, subject to applicable implementation changes. Transaction data reporting (e-reporting) applies to relevant business-to-consumer and cross-border transactions. Public-sector invoices must generally be submitted through Chorus Pro. Invoices must satisfy French VAT content, authenticity, integrity, and archiving requirements; France does not generally require a government digital stamp for each invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT when the supplier holds the export customs declaration and evidence that the goods exited the EU, subject to the applicable French General Tax Code conditions. Services are generally governed by place-of-supply rules rather than a generic export zero rate: B2B services supplied to a business established outside France are commonly outside the scope of French VAT, while specified financial and payment services may be VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated. A corporate virtual-card issuer must distinguish exempt payment execution or credit-related services from taxable software, program-management, data, support, and other ancillary services. VAT refunds require valid invoices, customs evidence where applicable, proof of business use, and reconciliation to accounting and VAT returns.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration and customs MRN or equivalent export reference
Customs exit confirmation or equivalent evidence that the goods left the European Union
Commercial invoice, packing list, and transport document such as bill of lading, air waybill, or consignment note
Proof of delivery or destination evidence where required by the transaction and audit circumstances
Customer and supplier VAT identification data, contractual documentation, and VAT return reconciliation
Inward remittance evidence may support commercial substantiation but is not generally a universal statutory condition for French export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. The DGFiP may assess unpaid VAT, interest for late payment, and penalties where export conditions or exemption evidence are not substantiated. The principal penalty may be 40% for deliberate failure and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law, subject to statutory qualification and procedural safeguards; a 10% surcharge may apply for late payment or certain filing failures. Fraudulent VAT refund claims can be denied, clawed back with interest and penalties, and referred for criminal prosecution. Tax fraud may result in imprisonment and substantial fines, with enhanced sanctions in aggravated cases and potentially higher corporate penalties. Records, customs evidence, invoices, contracts, payment records, and VAT reconciliations should be retained for the applicable French accounting and tax limitation periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates within the Eurozone, ensuring full convertibility and free movement of the Euro for capital and current account transactions. Non-Euro currency transactions are subject to mandatory reporting to the Banque de France under EU Regulation 2018/1672. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted without prior authorization provided they comply with corporate tax residency rules and do not exceed declared dividends; large or unusual remittances require supporting documentation to prevent capital flight classification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: French exporters must repatriate export proceeds within six months of shipment date. Mandatory conversion to Euro occurs at the official ECB reference rate. All receipts require prior customs declaration via Douane and subsequent reporting to tax authorities (DGFiP) via the e-BAC system. Banks enforce surrender through account verification and may impose penalties for non-compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Legal constraints include mandatory acquisition of a Payment Institution license from the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) under MiCA and PSD2 frameworks. Virtual card issuance requires explicit regulatory approval and segregation of client funds; offshore digital EMIs are restricted without French entity licensing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors or authorized signatories is mandatory for initial corporate onboarding and face-to-face KYC interviews at the bank branch. Subsequent remote video verification via secure platforms is permitted for ongoing transactions once core onboarding is complete.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership exceeding 25% in high-risk jurisdictions or PEP status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declaration, source of wealth certificate, corporate ownership chart, and independent legal opinion on non-shell status

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained large inbound capital injections or cross-border wire patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction narrative, export contract evidence, bank reference letters, and tax residency proof

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent financial statements or virtual card spend anomalies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financials, card usage reports, and third-party compliance attestation

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocols utilize SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY'. Verification requires incorporation certificate, shareholder agreement, and beneficial ownership declaration. All transfers must reference the French SAS entity ID and include tax identification number (SIREN/SIRET). Banks perform automated screening against OFAC, UN, and EU sanctions lists.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails include SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers and Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) processed through correspondent banks in EUR or USD. Trade settlements require matching purchase orders, invoices, and proof of goods shipment. Purpose codes must align with commercial activity; FX conversion occurs at interbank rates with full audit trail.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats / liasse fiscale, Form 2065 and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year closed 31 December: 3 May of the following year when filed online; 15 May for paper filing. For non-calendar fiscal years: within 3 months of fiscal year-end, with a 15-day extension for online filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of tax due (40% for bad faith, 80% for fraudulent conduct) plus late-payment interest of 0.2% per month. Failure to file triggers administrative assessment (taxation d'office) under Article L65 of the French Tax Procedures Code.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and financial statements deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) and INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the end of the fiscal year. For calendar-year accounts, due by 31 July. Extension may be requested by court order for a maximum of 6 additional months.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 1,500 (EUR 3,000 on repeated violation) for each document; court may order filing under coercive (astreinte) payments; failure to deposit for 3 consecutive years can trigger administrative strike-off and loss of legal protections.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of beneficial owners (UBO / déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via RCS / Infogreffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers. If no change, no standalone annual filing is required, but the UBO information is confirmed in the annual accounts deposit due within 7 months of fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 7,500 for the legal representative and EUR 37,500 for the legal entity for failure to file or update; imprisonment up to 6 months for deliberately false UBO declarations; publication of sanctions may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual regulatory filing to ACPR for licensed payment/e-money institution (prudential returns and audited financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end, in practice by 30 April following the close; specific COREP/FINREP reports follow deadlines set in ACPR/European delegated regulations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ACPR may impose formal warnings, reprimands, administrative sanctions, fines up to EUR 1,000,000, restrictions on authorization, and ultimately withdrawal of the e-money/payment institution license for persistent non-reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer payroll social declaration (DSN annual closing event and certificate of employee tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: URSSAF and other social security agencies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual closing DSN declaration is due within 30 days after the issuance of employee income tax certificates, generally by 31 January of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the social security contributions due, increased to 10% after 30 days; late-payment interest of 1.5% per month plus additional fines; employer surcharge may be imposed if no filing is made.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when exceeding any two of the following three thresholds: total balance-sheet assets greater than EUR 4,000,000; net turnover greater than EUR 8,000,000; average employee count greater than 50. In addition, for ISIC 6619 (virtual card issuing), ACPR-licensed payment and e-money institutions are subject to mandatory statutory audit regardless of these thresholds under Article L. 612-44 of the French Monetary and Financial Code.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général under ANC regulations) for individual statutory financial statements; IFRS as adopted by the EU for consolidated financial statements; ACPR prudential returns may require IFRS-derived reporting templates.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a standalone annual UBO renewal. The UBO declaration is filed at incorporation and must be updated within 30 days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership. At the time of the annual accounts deposit (within 7 months of fiscal year-end), the company must confirm that the UBO information on file remains accurate; if any change occurred during the year, a new declaration must be filed within 30 days of that change. The annual confirmation is therefore embedded in the annual filing cycle, and a failure to maintain accurate UBO data may be treated as a missed update.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des décisions et des procès-verbaux (minute book of shareholder and director decisions)
Registre des mouvements de titres (statutory share transfer register)
Registre des actes et dépôts sociaux (corporate acts and statutory filings log)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 130–USD 1,620 per annum depending on service tier; basic domiciliation in France typically ranges EUR 120–EUR 350 (USD 130–USD 420); premium registered office for regulated fintechs typically ranges EUR 500–EUR 1,500 (USD 540–USD 1,620).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500–USD 45,000 based on scope and complexity; simple SAS statutory audit generally EUR 5,000–EUR 12,000 (USD 5,500–USD 13,200); fintech with ACPR prudential reporting and group consolidation generally EUR 15,000–EUR 45,000 (USD 16,000–USD 49,000).

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced corporate income tax rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs meeting Article 219-I-b CGI conditions; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100m; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20%; Patent Box optional reduced rate of 10% on qualifying IP income; Young Innovative Company (JEI) exemptions for R&D-intensive SMEs. Tax losses are carried forward indefinitely but annual utilisation is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding that threshold; three-year carryback is available up to EUR 1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571-SD (declaration de resultats) and the liasse fiscale schedules 2050 to 2059, submitted electronically through the GECI/EFI portal at impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, accompanied by quarterly corporate income tax instalments due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; the final balance is due at the annual filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years ending on 31 December, the annual return and balance payment are due by the second working day following 1 May. For off-calendar fiscal years, the return is due within three months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: SIREN, SIRET, APE/NAF code, legal form, registered office, fiscal year opening and closing dates, tax identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the shareholding structure and indicate if any shareholder is a non-resident. The French SAS itself files as a French tax resident; no separate non-resident return is required for the entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result computed from statutory accounts: book profit, tax adjustments, prior-year loss offsets, special deductions and reinstatements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The profit before tax must be computed in accordance with French GAAP as adjusted by the tax schedules (2058-A and 2058-B). No deduction is available solely because shareholders are non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Table 2058-A - Transfer pricing and CFC adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares intercompany transactions, payments made to non-residents, transfer pricing adjustments, foreign tax debits, anti-abuse recharacterisations and CFC income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a virtual card issuer with foreign related treasury, processing, licensing or financing entities, the arm's length price of each transaction must be fully documented and reported; the non-resident beneficiary's tax residence is used to determine treaty protection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of corporate income tax at the 15% reduced rate for eligible small enterprises and at the 25% standard rate for the balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced rate remains available for a French SAS held by non-residents provided the company itself meets the French statutory conditions (fully paid-up capital, turnover under EUR 10m, and no more than 75% held by legal entities not themselves subject to IS).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory balance sheet with intangible assets, financial assets, receivables, borrowings and shareholder loans.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loans and balances with foreign related companies must be itemised. For a card issuer, software, card scheme licences and platform development costs should be capitalised or expensed consistently with arm's length practice.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% penalty on the net tax due if filed within 30 days of the statutory deadline, 40% if filed after formal notice, and 80% for intentional fraud or false statements. Late payment: monthly late-payment interest at 0.2% of the outstanding tax plus an additional 10% penalty for non-payment by the deadline. The tax administration may impose a fixed EUR 150 fine for failure to submit itemised schedules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% under Article 119-bis-2 CGI for dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders, reduced to 0% for qualifying corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (direct or indirect holding of at least 10% for at least two years); most tax treaties provide a reduced rate of 15% for portfolio dividends and 5% for direct investment dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from a reduced dividend withholding tax rate, the non-resident shareholder must file an application with the French tax authorities using Form 5002 (if treaty-based), Form 5013 (if the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies), or the relevant simplified certificate, together with a certificate of tax residence for the fiscal year in question. The forms must be delivered to the paying company and the French tax office before or at the time of distribution. If full withholding has been applied, a reclaim may be filed with the local DRFIP within the statutory period (normally by 31 December of the second year following the year of income).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: France applies a statutory withholding of 30% on interest and debt instrument income paid to non-resident individuals, but arm's length interest paid to non-resident corporate creditors is generally exempt from withholding when the creditor is the beneficial owner and a treaty resident; the EU Interest & Royalties Directive reduces the withholding to 0% for associated EU companies with a direct holding of at least 25%. Royalties: the domestic withholding rate on industrial property royalties paid to non-residents is 33.33%; most tax treaties reduce the rate to 0% to 10%, and the EU Interest & Royalties Directive provides a 0% rate for qualifying affiliated EU companies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 - full Local File and Master File documentation is mandatory for enterprises whose consolidated turnover or gross assets exceed EUR 400 million for the fiscal year under Article L.13 AA of the French Book of Tax Procedure. Below this threshold, proportionate contemporaneous documentation must still be produced on request to support the arm's length character of intercompany transactions.
